topic: Human Respiratory, Circulatory, and Nervous Systems
key_concepts: Respiration is the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide with the environment.
The nasal cavity uses hairs and sticky mucus to trap dust and other impurities from inhale
The pharynx is a common passageway for food, water, and air.
The larynx contains vocal cords that vibrate when air passes by them.
The trachea, or windpipe, filters inhaled air and branches into the bronchi.
The bronchi are two tubes that carry air into the lungs.
Bronchioles are smaller tubes that branch off into alveoli.

The lungs are the main organs of the respiratory system where gas exchange occurs.
The diaphragm is a dome-shaped muscle that controls breathing by contracting and relaxing.
The heart pumps blood through blood vessels throughout the body.
